title: Separate pre-install bootstrap from installed update routing

requirement.summary: Use the exact-wheel guided-next rehearsal to decide where installation and update guidance belong without fabricating a self-installing CLI or an unpublished release.

objective.rationale: A CLI cannot inspect the state before it is installed, while update routing cannot be truthful or progress-making without reviewed release metadata and an explicit precedence contract.

goal: Record the bootstrap/update ownership boundary, retain the existing read-only installed update check, and define gates that must be met before update availability may enter agentgov next.
non_goals: Do not change next_action.py, update_check.py, CLI arguments, schemas, release metadata, package identity, install behavior, update execution, or repository refresh behavior.
Do not invent a 0.3 wheel URL, digest, stable manifest, release candidate, package-index entry, or automatic discovery service.
Do not download, install, upgrade, uninstall, refresh, migrate a consumer, or create or modify a workflow.
Do not add an acknowledgement file, update event, hook, daemon, background check, notification, or telemetry.
Do not commit in the AgentGov source repository, push, tag, publish, release, merge, deploy, or mutate an external system.
Preserve all earlier uncommitted bounded slices and report their combined working-copy scope honestly.
acceptance_signals: The decision states that pre-install bootstrap is owned by a reviewed public installation surface because agentgov next cannot run before AgentGov exists.
Stable installation remains an isolated pipx command pinned to a fixed release wheel; development-source commands remain explicitly separate and are not presented as a stable release.
Installed update inspection remains the existing read-only agentgov update --check surface and grants no install or repository-write authority.
The current development manifest with channel development and artifact null cannot produce or justify a tool-update action.

Future next integration is blocked until a reviewed stable manifest supplies a newer compatible version, fixed-tag HTTPS wheel URL and SHA-256, a no-active-session rule, deterministic precedence, and a non-looping progress contract.
Current next and update code, schemas, release metadata, CLI behavior, and stable public commands remain unchanged.
Documentation tests protect the bootstrap ownership, no-fabricated-release, read-only update check, no-active-session, and no-execution boundaries.
The full source suite and repository governance checks pass.

items: Documentation could imply that next can observe a pre-install state or that an unpublished 0.3 artifact exists.
A future update recommendation could displace an active task or loop forever if its read-only observation cannot change state.
The stable install path and development-source identity could be conflated.

stop_conditions: Stop if the decision requires changing runtime behavior, release metadata, a workflow, or an external installation surface.
Stop if no trustworthy non-looping state transition can be specified for a future next update recommendation.
Stop if any wording implies that development source 0.3.0.dev0 is a published installable release.
Stop if update routing would interrupt an active governed development session or weaken existing onboarding, repository-failure, and human-confirmation boundaries.

decision.rationale: The user explicitly authorized the recommended bootstrap/update boundary decision after the installed guided-next rehearsal. The delivered task was paused on 2026-08-05 to remove it from automatic discovery; this is routing hygiene, not a claim of semantic completion, acceptance, merge, or release.
